title: A two-mode numerical prediction and its limits
promptMarkdown: Build a standard-library Euler simulation for two independent balanced modes with targets s=(3,1), q₀=(0.01,0.01), factors a=b=√q₀, dt=0.001 and duration3. Use the specified loss½Σ(q_i−s_i)² and simultaneous factor updates. Compare against q_i (t)=s_i/[1+(s_i/q_i0−1) e^(−2s_it)] at t=1,2,3; rerun dt/2. Treat e₁, e₂ as the two training inputs to T=diag(3,1), and (1,1),(1,−1) as fixed prediction checks. Report predictions and squared errors at t=3, explain why these checks are not an independent population-generalisation estimate, and state the assumptions behind mode separation. Include code, not only numbers.
hintLadder: Reuse the single-mode factor update twice with independent scalar states.
Use q1x1, q2x2 to compute held-out-combination predictions.
Distinguish exact-flow error, numerical error and statistical generalisation error.
